# Policy and hook reference

<!-- codeflow-derived policy-reference begin: generated by codeflow from the binary; do not edit between the markers. Regenerate with CODEFLOW_REGENERATE_LOOKUPS=1 cargo test -p codeflow-cli derived_lookup -->

Every key `.codeflow/policy.json` accepts, with its type, built-in default and valid values. A missing file or key means the default applies; `codeflow policy show` prints the values in effect for a repository.

Level keys accept `off`, `warn`, `allow` or `block`: block = violations stop the operation; warn = violations are reported and the operation proceeds; allow = explicitly permitted; off = the check is not run. `allow` and `off` are BOTH inactive; only warn/block enforce.

## Top-level keys

| Key | Type | Default | Valid values | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | uint | `0` | a non-negative integer | Version of the policy.json schema. | The scaffold writes 1; the loader does not read or migrate on it today (inert). |
| `human_authorization` | enum | `none` | none | Out-of-band human-authorization mode for irreversible actions (ADR-0009). | Only `none` exists today: an inert seam for future totp/push/webauthn adapters. |

## Git keys

| Key | Type | Default | Valid values | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `git.protected_branches` | string list | `["main","master"]` | an array of branch names or glob patterns (e.g. release/*) | Branches every enforcement plane treats as protected. | Globs use the `glob` crate's syntax; read by all four planes. |
| `git.commit_to_protected` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | A commit made directly on a protected branch. |  |
| `git.push_to_protected` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | A push to a protected branch. |  |
| `git.force_push_protected` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | A force-push to a protected branch. |  |
| `git.force_push_unprotected` | Level | `allow` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | A force-push to a NON-protected branch. | The only non-strict default (allow); it sanctions the durability push with --force-with-lease; set block to forbid. |
| `git.delete_protected` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Deleting a protected branch. |  |
| `git.hard_reset_protected` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | A hard reset on a protected branch. |  |
| `git.merge_to_protected` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | A merge commit landing on a protected branch. | PR merge and `codeflow integrate` are the sanctioned paths; a human may override the git layer with CODEFLOW_HUMAN_OVERRIDE=1. |
| `git.pr_merge_to_protected` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | A `gh pr merge` whose base branch is protected (git-guard only). |  |
| `git.local_ref_protection` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Any local update of a protected ref that did not come from the remote. | The reference-transaction backstop (ADR-0007): catches fast-forward merges, reset --hard, and branch -D that classic client hooks miss. |
| `git.hook_integrity` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Tampering with the enforcement plane itself (hooksPath flips, hook-skip envs, hook/policy writes). | git-guard only (ADR-0009); suspended only in the pre-first-commit bootstrap window. |
| `git.commit_format` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Conventional-commit subject shape: `type(scope): description`. | Governs three checks: commit_types, commit_desc_max_len, and commit_subject_max_len; off/allow disables all of them. |
| `git.commit_types` | string list | `["feat","fix","docs","refactor","test","chore","ci","perf","build","revert"]` | an array of lower-case conventional commit types | The whitelist of commit types. | Enforced under commit_format. |
| `git.commit_desc_max_len` | uint | `50` | a non-negative integer (character count) | Max length of the description, the text after `type(scope): `. | Enforced under commit_format. |
| `git.commit_subject_max_len` | uint | `72` | a non-negative integer (character count) | Max length of the whole subject line (git's 72-column wrap). | Enforced under commit_format. |
| `git.commit_body` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Shape of the commit body: only `- ` bullets, blank lines, and sanctioned footers. | Governs the whole body family: the bullet caps, footer tokens, required footers, and ticket trailers; off/allow disables them all. Merge/revert/fixup/squash commits are exempt. |
| `git.commit_body_max_bullets` | uint | `3` | a non-negative integer | Max number of `- ` bullets allowed in a commit body. | Enforced under commit_body. |
| `git.commit_body_bullet_max_len` | uint | `72` | a non-negative integer (character count, including the `- ` marker) | Max length of a single commit-body bullet line. | Enforced under commit_body. |
| `git.commit_footer_tokens` | string list | `[]` | an array of exact, case-sensitive trailer tokens (e.g. Signed-off-by) | Footer trailers ALLOWED (optional) beyond the always-allowed BREAKING CHANGE:. | Unioned with commit_required_footers and commit_ticket_keys into the sanctioned-footer set; enforced under commit_body. |
| `git.commit_required_footers` | string list | `[]` | an array of exact, case-sensitive trailer tokens (e.g. Signed-off-by) | Footer trailers that MUST appear on every non-exempt commit (e.g. DCO). | A required token is implicitly allowed; a commit missing one blocks under commit_body. |
| `git.commit_ticket_keys` | string list | `[]` | an array of exact, case-sensitive trailer tokens (e.g. Refs, Closes) | Ticket-reference trailer tokens the project recognizes. | EMPTY = the ticket feature is off and a `Refs:` line BLOCKS unless listed in commit_footer_tokens; non-empty allows these tokens and arms commit_ticket_required. |
| `git.commit_ticket_required` | Level | `off` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Whether a matching ticket-reference trailer is REQUIRED on every commit. | Only meaningful when commit_ticket_keys is non-empty; `allow` behaves like `off` here (inactive); use warn or block to require. Merge/revert/fixup/squash commits are exempt. |
| `git.commit_ticket_pattern` | string | `""` | a regular expression, e.g. ^PROJ-\d+$ (empty = no format check) | Regex a present ticket trailer's value must match. | Strictly validated: an unparseable pattern is a loud error at the commit-msg hook, `codeflow ci`, and `codeflow validate` (at enforcement time it would silently fail open). |
| `git.breaking_watch_paths` | string list | `[]` | an array of path globs (the `glob` crate's syntax) | Declared contract surfaces: an unmarked commit touching one draws a WARN. | Warn-only, never blocks, whatever the levels say; empty = no tripwire. The nudge asks for a `type!:` marker or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer. |
| `git.ai_attribution` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | AI attribution (Co-Authored-By AI trailers, "Generated with", robot emoji) in commits and PR bodies. |  |
| `git.commit_emoji` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Emoji in commit subjects and PR bodies. |  |
| `git.policy_characters` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | En and em dashes (U+2013, U+2014) in commit messages, PR bodies, and lines a ci range adds under the written-content trees (ADR-0067). | Judges new text only: `codeflow ci` checks lines the range adds under docs/, project-management/ and the skill trees, so existing bytes are grandfathered and nothing asks for a sweep. |
| `git.pr_sections` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Required sections in the PR/MR body: the structure check `codeflow ci` runs on a provided PR body. | Governs pr_required_sections and pr_code_sections; off/allow disables both. PR events require a non-empty body; local/push runs without one skip. Presentation and template-remnant checks always warn, never block. |
| `git.pr_release_impact` | Level | `warn` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Generic Release impact fields and breaking commit floor in PR bodies. | Defaults to warn independently of pr_sections. Extra project fields are allowed; this check does not calculate versions or require release automation. |
| `git.pr_breaking_level` | enum | `major` | patch \| minor \| major | Minimum impact level permitted for Breaking: yes in the project's release policy. | Defaults to major. Pre-1.0 projects explicitly choose their level, commonly minor. Breaking commit markers floor Impact at this level. |
| `git.pr_required_sections` | string list | `["Summary","Changes"]` | an array of heading names without the leading ## (e.g. Summary) | Headings every PR body must carry, matched case-insensitively at ##/### depth. | A present-but-empty section (only HTML comments and bare `-` bullets) counts as missing; enforced under pr_sections. Fresh installs also list Reviews and Release impact; without this key the built-in default stays Summary and Changes. |
| `git.pr_code_sections` | string list | `["Testing"]` | an array of heading names without the leading ## (e.g. Testing) | Headings required only when the commit range touches non-docs files. | Docs-only = every changed path is *.md, *.txt, LICENSE*, docs/**, or a .github template; anything else, or a range whose files could not be resolved, counts as code. Enforced under pr_sections. |
| `git.branch_naming` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Branch names must match `{prefix}/{kebab-name}` with a sanctioned prefix. | Protected branches are exempt (governed by the protection rules, not naming); prefixes come from branch_prefixes. |
| `git.branch_prefixes` | string list | `["feat/","fix/","docs/","refactor/","test/","chore/","ci/","hotfix/","plan/","task/","spike/","experiment/","integration/"]` | an array of prefixes, each ending with `/` (e.g. feat/) | The sanctioned branch-name prefixes. | A prefix missing its trailing `/` never matches a `{prefix}/{name}` branch. |
| `git.secret_scan` | Level | `block` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Pre-commit scan for staged secrets and .env files. | Never suspended by bootstrap grace, but off/allow HERE does disable the scan (it is policy, not hardcoded); leave at block. |
| `git.test_gate_on_push` | Level | `warn` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Run the test gate before a push (pre-push hook). |  |
| `git.security_review` | Level | `warn` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | The umbrella gate for the CI security-review job. | Ships at warn (ADR-0016); harden to block when ready. |
| `git.dep_audit` | Level | `warn` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | The dependency-audit gate in CI. | Ships at warn (ADR-0016); harden to block when ready. |

## Security keys

| Key | Type | Default | Valid values | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `security.dangerous_commands` | enum | `block` | block | Destructive commands the exec-guard catches (rm -rf on system paths, dd to devices, mkfs, fork bombs). | Non-relaxable safety floor: stale or hand-edited weaker values are ignored by enforcement and rejected by validation. |
| `security.privilege_escalation` | Level | `warn` | off \| warn \| allow \| block | Privilege escalation the exec-guard catches (Unix sudo/su/doas/pkexec, Windows gsudo/runas/elevated PowerShell, LD_PRELOAD/PATH injection). | Default warn, not block: the harness's ask tier owns sudo prompting; the guard only surfaces in-session feedback. |

<!-- codeflow-derived policy-reference end -->

## Git hook stages

The five stages `codeflow git-hook` dispatches. Each shim in
`.codeflow/git-hooks/` runs its stage against the policy above. The stage
names are checked against the binary's dispatcher; the descriptions are
written here.

| Stage | What it checks | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `pre-commit` | A commit on a protected branch, and staged secrets or `.env` files | [git client hooks](architecture/enforcement-planes.md#git-client-hooks) |
| `commit-msg` | Commit format, AI attribution and emoji in the message | [git client hooks](architecture/enforcement-planes.md#git-client-hooks) |
| `pre-merge-commit` | A merge commit onto a protected branch that is not a fast forward | [git client hooks](architecture/enforcement-planes.md#git-client-hooks) |
| `reference-transaction` | A fast-forward merge, hard reset or branch delete on a protected branch | [git client hooks](architecture/enforcement-planes.md#git-client-hooks) |
| `pre-push` | A push, force-push or delete to a protected branch, and branch naming | [git client hooks](architecture/enforcement-planes.md#git-client-hooks) |
